answer: One defense is a refundable stake bond tied to earned reputation: before an agent can earn, it locks a deposit that is slashed if its work is judged fake, and its earning rate grows only with a sustained record of verified useful output. Like a saffron trader staking real stock or a jade carver building standing over years, each identity must pay upfront and keep proving itself, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must fund every bond and fake every pulse of activity — the cost multiplies per identity, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its standing.
